title: -FOP—SEGRET
summary: A declassified 1956-era Strategic Air Command study on strategic air warfare for 1959. It covers SAC's mission to conduct global atomic/nuclear operations against the Soviet bloc, with two tasks: win the Air Power Battle by destroying Soviet air power, then systematically destroy war-supporting resources. It explains targeting (ROME, BRAVO, DELTA objectives), target categories (air forces, air bases, atomic stockpiles, control centers, aircraft industry), prioritization criteria (USSR, China, satellites), and notes that target listings were consolidated under SAC Letter 129-56.

title: —FOP—SECREF—
summary: A declassified 1950s-era SAC (Strategic Air Command) target study describes the SAC target system: about 5,975 targets, including 1,602 SAC targets, with SAM sites and other categories excluded from the count. Targets are prioritized, with duplicated strikes limited to high-priority targets to avoid wasted effort. It references force-structure revisions (SIOP-related documents), notes operational factors based on intelligence and reliability assumptions, and mentions a breakdown of target categories and a yield/reliability analysis. The text is OCR-garbled and partially illegible.

title: —F O R - GEGREF— 0
summary: Declassified OCR text, largely garbled, about operational factors for weapon yield and CEP for BRL computation, and total requirement computations (gross error, budget, attrition, reliability, loss average factor). Lists bomber and missile systems (e.g., Minuteman/Mk series, W-38 warhead references) and notes reserve weapons assigned to targets, including projected DGZs versus existing ones. Describes general targeting guidelines: highest-yield weapons assigned to Air Power Bottleneck targets (airfields, launch sites, control centers, air industry, electronic industry, stockpile, missile sites) to ensure damage criteria, economize force, and reduce sorties.

title: —FOP—SECRET__
summary: A declassified, OCR-garbled 1950s-era US Air Force targeting document on nuclear weapons employment. It covers: high-yield weapons used against air power and offensive targets; Satellite targets assigned atomic weapons, with multiple/compound effects used only where damage criteria require; targeting based on maximum damage with minimum weapon yield and stockpile/operational constraints; damage criteria (runway cratering, underground and above-ground structure collapse, 90% probability of damage for satellite-area targets, 70% for others, collapse of industrial structures); and height-of-burst guidance favoring low bursts (about 1200 feet) for collapse effects, with air bursts reducing blast effect on certain targets.

title: ~ToP—-sEeRET—
summary: A declassified, OCR-garbled 1950s-era US nuclear targeting document discussing the Air Power Battle. Covers: surface versus air bursts and fallout tradeoffs (air bursts preferred to limit fallout, surface bursts accepted only where fallout risk to friendly forces is acceptable); height of burst for satellite and low-yield targets; weapon allocation by target value, size, type, and hardness; multiple-weapon attacks for destruction probability, with timing constraints precluding reliance on reattack; alternate weapons and aircraft; RASCAL and penetration aids; stockpile composition for Parts I and II; and a target category table covering airfields, headquarters, depots, missile sites, industry, and control centers.

title: TOTAL OPALIOY BR (Xe)
summary: A declassified, heavily OCR-garbled U.S. nuclear strategic-targeting document (TOP SECRET, marked declassified) covering attack options and weapons requirements. It includes a Part II target list grouped into categories: atomic forces, defense forces, atomic industry, control centers, and military industry, plus systematic destruction of supporting resources, stockpile sites, SAM sites, and ICBM sites. It also gives totals for DGZs, bomb weapons, and SAC requirements, and discusses destruction of DGZs with and without base-loss consideration.
